result:
The main thing stopping people is probably the subscription itself, not the bread. A weekly €18 commitment is a lot to sign up for when you haven't tasted it. I'd remove that risk first, then make the first box easy to say yes to.

## 1. Sell a single "try one Saturday" box (do this first)
- Sell one box with no subscription, at €18 or a little less (say €15).
- When it arrives, include a card: "Liked it? Subscribe this week and your first subscribed box is €X off" or "…and get a free pastry."
- This is cheap to run. You're already doing a Saturday route, so one extra drop within 3 km costs very little.
- Keep track of how many trial customers subscribe within 2 weeks. If 30–40% or more do, it's working.

## 2. Make leaving visibly easy
Put "Pause or cancel anytime, no fees" next to the price everywhere: on the website, on flyers and at the shop counter. People commit more readily when they know they can get out. If cancelling currently means a phone call or an email back-and-forth, make it a single link or a single message.

## 3. Let your 140 subscribers do the recruiting
This is the best use of a €300 budget. Ideas:
- **Referral:** a friend's first box is free or half price, and the subscriber gets a free pastry or €5 off. You only pay when it works.
- **"Bring a neighbour" card:** add a spare voucher to the box now and then that subscribers can hand to someone on their street. Your delivery area is small, so word of mouth spreads fast there.

## 4. Use the shop as a tasting room
- On weekdays, put out samples of the bread-box loaves with a sign reading "This is what comes in Saturday's box."
- Add a QR code or a paper sign-up sheet for the trial box right next to the samples.
- People who already buy in the shop are the easiest to convert, so make sure they know the box exists.

## 5. Remove small points of friction
- Put a "Do you deliver to my street?" check (map or postcode list) on the sign-up page so people don't have to email to find out.
- Show what's in a typical box with photos, and include allergen info.
- Accept payment the way locals expect to pay (card, and whatever local payment apps are common).
- Offer pickup at the shop for people just outside the 3 km zone or who aren't home on Saturday mornings.

## 6. Seasonal gift box
A "gift a Saturday box" option before the holidays and on occasions like Mother's Day works as a trial too. The recipient tastes the bread without having chosen to commit, and the giver is effectively recommending you.

---

**If you only do two things:** launch the one-off trial box with a conversion card inside, and start a referral offer for current subscribers. Both cost little up front, you only spend money when someone actually tries the box, and you can tell within a month whether they're working.

One thing to check before discounting: what does each box cost you to make and deliver? That tells you how cheap the trial box can go. If you share it, I can work out a trial price and referral reward that still pay off.
